findings.title: S-102.1/.2 print the flat-roof snow load as 35 psf at Ct=1.0 for the UNHEATED canopy and garage; the house's own basis and the truss order say 42 psf (Ct=1.2) plus drift

evidence.measured: S-102.1 and S-102.2 note 4: 'GROUND SNOW LOAD Pg = 50 PSF; FLAT-ROOF Pf = 35 PSF AT Ce = Ct = Is = 1.0'. _snow_load_note prints 0.7 x Pg for every roof with the comment 'fully-exposed, heated'. A-593 says the garage attic is 'vented, unconditioned'; the canopy is an open, unheated roof. The truss-order annotation (garage.py:877, printed on the truss sheets' source) states 'flat 42 psf balanced' and the roof-step drift; north_entry_piers.md s.3 line 127 derives p_f = 0.7(1.0)(1.2)(1.0)(50) = 42 psf with 'C_t = 1.2 because this is an unheated open canopy'. The fabricator therefore receives two flat-roof numbers (35 vs 42 psf) on one permit set. RF-HOUSE (heated, 35 psf) is correct.
evidence.expected: Each roof sheet states the flat-roof snow at that roof's own thermal factor: 42 psf (Ct 1.2) for the canopy and the unheated garage, 35 psf for the house, or no number at all and a pointer to the truss order. ASCE 7-16 Table 7.3-2 Ct for unheated structures is the source the house note already cites; not re-quoted here.
evidence.method: Read note 4 on pp.14-16 of permit_set_full.pdf; read _snow_load_note in roofframingplan.py:299-307; compare north_entry_piers.md:127-134 and garage.py:877.
